frequency_question: How often is a nomination successfully reported out of committee and confirmed by a recorded floor vote within 8 calendar days of initial formal receipt when assuming full institutional and political cooperation?
membership_rule: Includes any executive branch nomination officially received by the Senate where floor action concluded within 8 calendar days. Excludes nominations that sat in committee past the 8-day threshold due to mandatory statutory waiting periods or hearings that cannot be waived.

cases.name: Fast-track executive/judicial appointments under unanimous consent agreements
Nominations requiring standard committee notice waivers and floor cloture invocation

provenance_note: claims 120 cases from only 2 named (60.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 2 named procedural pathways identified; estimated fewer than 5 instances total across recent Congresses where a full nomination cycle completed in 8 days or less without pre-arranged emergency consensus.
known_gaps: Excludes emergency recesses and instances where nominations were formally held at the desk.
skeleton: Committee notice rule (Rule XXVI requires a minimum of 6 days' notice unless waived) multiplied by floor cloture filing requirements (Rule XXII requires 2 days of intervening time after cloture is filed before a vote can occur).
multiplier: 6 days minimum committee notice + 2 days minimum floor cloture = 8 absolute minimum calendar days under standard contested rules, assuming zero delay, zero debate time, and immediate unanimous consent to waive all additional waiting periods.
validity_reason: Senate standing rules on committee notice and cloture procedures remain fixed across congressional terms unless amended by resolution.
